analysis.title: NVIDIA Corp: Media Reports on CEO Change; A Few Thoughts (First Read)
key_insights: Media reports say NVDA's Board is preparing to oust Jensen Huang as CEO and is working with an outside firm to identify successor candidates. UBS expects the company would find a strong candidate, but sees Huang as a singular force and expects the impact to be felt widely.

Financing risk: NVDA has become a key source of funds for neo-clouds, LLM developers, ecosystem partners and suppliers, and UBS sees Huang as the driving force behind this. Even if a new CEO keeps the approach, UBS expects a near-term pause in the company's willingness and ability to do these deals.

UBS estimates NVDA generates ~$50-60B per quarter in FCF, with a big portion put back into the AI ecosystem. A pause could remove ~$50B or more from the system, at least temporarily, while interest rates are rising and parts of the credit market have become less liquid.
Supply chain risk: NVDA has been far ahead of peers in long-term supply agreements for memory, substrates and other inputs. UBS saw Huang as singular and out in front of key peers on procurement.

Regulatory risk: the US government could enforce tighter restrictions on NVDA's (and AMD's) ability to ship product to China, and more importantly to regions such as Singapore or Malaysia. Singapore was nearly 20% of revenue when NVDA changed its geographic disclosure in mid-C2025.
UBS estimates roughly 10% of revenue could be at risk if a portion of Singapore revenue plus some additional portion of the now small China revenue were restricted.
UBS says longer-term issues such as the product roadmap go beyond the CEO and any impact would take years to show up.
Rating Buy, PT $300 unchanged, based on ~14x C2028E P/E applied to C2028E EPS of $22.08 (unchanged). Price was $173.73 on 11 Nov 2026, implying 72.7% forecast price appreciation.
UBS EPS estimates are above consensus: FY 01/27E $9.57 vs $9.30, 01/28E $17.16 vs $15.86, 01/29E $22.08 vs $21.05. Q3E $2.53 vs cons $2.48, Q4E $2.95 vs cons $2.75.
UBS revenue estimates: $420.3B (01/27E), $744.2B (01/28E), $985.1B (01/29E), then declining to $934.5B (01/30E) and $840.6B (01/31E).

market_movers.rationale: PT unchanged at $300 (~14x C2028E EPS of $22.08) despite reports of a possible CEO change. UBS flags near-term risks to AI financing, supply chain and export restrictions.

earnings_insights: UBS diluted EPS estimates (UBS estimates, not reported): Q3E FY01/27 $2.53 vs consensus $2.48, Q4E $2.95 vs consensus $2.75. Q1 $1.87 and Q2 $2.22 are reported and in line with consensus.
UBS FY 01/27E EPS $9.57 vs consensus $9.30, FY 01/28E $17.16 vs consensus $15.86, FY 01/29E $22.08 vs consensus $21.05.
UBS estimates NVDA FCF at ~$50-60B per quarter.
risk_factors: Pause in NVDA's AI ecosystem financing under new leadership, potentially removing ~$50B or more from the system while rates are rising and some credit segments are less liquid.
Loss of Huang's procurement influence in long-term supply agreements for memory and substrates.
Tighter US export restrictions affecting China, Singapore and Malaysia, with about 10% of revenue potentially at risk (UBS estimate).
Longer-term product roadmap uncertainty, though UBS expects any impact to take years to appear.
Company-specific risks listed: AMD competition in GPUs, ARM-based applications processors competition, and Intel's MIC processors.
geopolitical: The US government could enforce tighter restrictions on NVDA and AMD shipments to China and to Singapore or Malaysia.

tension_points.bull_case: The company would likely find a strong successor, a new leader may keep the financing approach, and the impact beyond the CEO would take years to show up. UBS keeps Buy and a $300 PT.
tension_points.bear_case: Huang is a singular force. A near-term pause in ecosystem financing could take ~$50B or more out of the system, procurement advantages could weaken, and tighter export rules could put ~10% of revenue at risk.

theme_stances.key_argument: Huang's removal would likely pause AI ecosystem financing, weaken supply chain positioning and raise export restriction risk near term.
theme_stances.evidence: we always viewed Jensen as somewhat singular in this regard
